panels.rationale: Human skin histopathology shows the characteristic non-caseating granulomatous infiltrate with multinucleated giant cells described in the caption for Blau syndrome.

panels.figure_caption: Granulomatous dermatitis. Inflammatory infiltrate of the subpapilar dermis with typical multinucleated giant cells within a non-caseating epithelioid cell Blau granuloma.
in_text_mentions: entation with a skin biopsy showing non-caseating granulomas [15]. Later the exanthema becomes tan-colored and may present a “dirty’ scaly appearance (Figure 3). The later stage of the rash tends to last longer and may constitute a valuable diagnostic clue. When a skin biopsy is performed a non-caseating granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate located in the dermis is characteristic (Figure 4). In the Blau international registry, the skin has offered better diagnostic yield when compared to synovium, with confirmatory histology in more than 90% of the patients eventually diagnosed with Blau [6].
